title: Astrophysics & Further Mechanics — SHM, Orbits & Cosmology
subject: physics

questions.prompt: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration is:
options: Proportional to displacement and directed towards equilibrium
Constant and directed along the motion
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — a = −ω²x: proportional to displacement, opposite sign (towards equilibrium).
questions.feedbackWrong: SHM's defining equation: a = −ω²x — acceleration proportional to displacement and directed back towards equilibrium.

mistakes.misconception: Places maximum acceleration where speed is maximum.
mistakes.correction: Acceleration is maximum at the EXTREMES (largest displacement) — and zero at equilibrium where speed peaks.

questions.prompt: A mass on a spring oscillates in SHM with angular frequency ω = 4.0 rad/s. Calculate the period of oscillation in seconds.
Describe how kinetic energy and potential energy vary during one full oscillation of a simple pendulum, and what happens to the total energy (neglecting damping).

markScheme.text: KE maximum at the equilibrium (lowest) point where speed is greatest; zero at the extremes.
PE maximum at the extremes (greatest height/displacement); minimum at equilibrium.
Total energy stays CONSTANT — energy continuously converts between kinetic and potential forms.

questions.prompt: Light from a distant galaxy is shifted towards longer wavelengths (redshift). This indicates the galaxy is:
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — recession stretches wavelengths: redshift means moving away.
questions.feedbackWrong: Redshift = stretching of wavelength = the source recedes. Approach would compress wavelengths (blueshift).

mistakes.misconception: Associates red with approach because red feels 'warmer/closer'.
mistakes.correction: Redshift means LONGER wavelength — the waves stretch as the source recedes. Blueshift is approach.

questions.prompt: A galaxy recedes at 1400 km/s. Using H₀ = 70 km/s/Mpc, estimate its distance in Mpc.
Outline the life cycle of a star similar in mass to the Sun, from nebula to final state.

markScheme.text: A nebula collapses under gravity, heating until hydrogen fusion ignites — a main-sequence star.
When hydrogen in the core is exhausted, the star expands into a red giant, fusing helium in the core.
Outer layers are ejected as a planetary nebula.
The remaining core becomes a white dwarf, cooling gradually — no further fusion since mass is too low to fuse heavier elements.

mistakes.misconception: Ends all stellar life cycles in supernova.
mistakes.correction: Sun-mass stars are far too small — supernovae require stars of roughly 8+ solar masses. Small stars fade as white dwarfs.

questions.prompt: State two pieces of evidence supporting the Big Bang model of the universe.

markScheme.text: Cosmic microwave background radiation — the redshifted afterglow of the hot early universe, uniform in all directions.
Hubble's redshift-distance relationship: galaxies recede faster the further they are — consistent with expansion from an initial state.
Also creditable: observed abundance of light elements (hydrogen/helium ratio) matches Big Bang nucleosynthesis predictions.

questions.prompt: A satellite orbits with a period of 2 hours at radius r. If the radius is increased to 4r, the period becomes 2 × 4^1.5 hours — enter this value in hours.

stepChecks.label: Kepler: $T^2 \propto r^3$, so T scales by $4^{1.5}$

questions.prompt: Stellar parallax measures distance to nearby stars using:
options: The apparent shift of a star against distant background as Earth orbits the Sun
The brightness of the star compared to the Sun
The time light takes to arrive
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the star appears to shift against distant background over Earth's orbit; the angle gives distance (1 parsec = 1 arcsec parallax).
questions.feedbackWrong: Parallax is geometric: Earth's orbital baseline creates an apparent shift; smaller shift = further star. Defines the parsec.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses parallax with the inverse-square brightness method.
mistakes.correction: Brightness methods need a known luminosity (standard candle); parallax is purely geometric triangulation.
